card.title: BREAKOUT
card.text: Give a Veteran unit Fury and Shock.
card.flavorText: A breakout is a military operation to end a situation where troops are surrounded by the enemy, by launching assaults that achieve a breakthrough: escape from confinement. Encircled forces face annihilation unless they are relieved or they manage to break out. In the fluid combat of WWII, it was common for large forces to get surrounded, like at Dunkirk, Stalingrad, Korsun or Falaise. Breakout attempts were dangerous and desperate affairs, but they were often the only hope of survival for a surrounded unit. Such desperation could lead to heroic and furious actions. British General Bernard Montgomery used breakout tactics most famously during the Battle of El Alamein in late 1942. This was a turning point in the North African Campaign of World War II. Montgomery concentrated his forces and firepower on a narrow front, breaking through German and Italian lines to perform a breakout. Montgomery was thus able to wear down Field Marshal Erwin Rommel's Afrika Korps, eventually forcing an Axis retreat.
